source: Staffordshire CC 2026/27 MTFS budget (ModernGov doc s205066, full Council Feb 2026, verified) + the AI DOGE directorate engine.

directorates.name: Health and Care
directorates._note: Largest directorate; carries the bulk of the savings.

cross_cutting._note: 2026/27 savings programme GBP 21.470m by directorate; the directorate engine risk-adjusts it to GBP 12.3m EV.

reserves._note: CIPFA resilience indicator: low risk on level and use of usable reserves; a GBP 3.688m contribution from reserves supports the 2026/27 budget. Usable reserves total not separately extracted.

risks.risk: DSG High Needs deficit GBP 53.6m at end 2024/25, High Needs Block overspend GBP 42m per year, forecast to exceed GBP 200m by the end of the MTFS if unmitigated, against a statutory override that ends 31 March 2028. Staffordshire has NO DfE Safety Valve agreement and manages the deficit through its own DSG Deficit Management Plan, so the cliff is severe.
Forward MTFP gap (Headroom/Shortfall) rising to GBP 11.030m (2027/28), GBP 25.163m (2028/29), GBP 49.329m (2029/30), GBP 59.780m (2030/31); as a shire county, funding reduces over the period.
Adult social care (Health and Care) carries GBP 13.974m of the GBP 21.470m savings, the bulk; delivery risk concentrated in ASC, with SEND stabilisation a stated pressure.
